title: Evaluating The Skill Mill programme to lower violence and offending in young people
official: The Skill Mill programme to reduce the risk of violence and offending: a two-armed randomised controlled trial with an internal pilot
summary:
Background and study aims 
The study has been commissioned by the Youth Endowment Fund (YEF) and involves an impact and process evaluation of The Skill Mill (TSM), an intervention targeted at young people (YP) aged 16-18 who have offended and referred to the Youth Offending Service (YOS). Involvement in violence and crime can have a major impact on YP, as both victims and perpetrators. Many of those involved have experienced challenging or traumatic events in their lives. Being involved in crime can lead to mental health problems, risky behaviours, and increased costs for health and justice systems. 
The Skill Mill is an intervention designed to address youth offending by providing at-risk YP with paid, six-month employment in environmental and practical work, alongside skills development. YP work in small crews under supervision, are paid weekly, and receive support to set up bank accounts and access statutory employment benefits. The programme includes practical and accredited training, wrap-around support in collaboration with YOS, and a three-month post-employment phase that helps participants secure further work, training, or education. The intervention focuses on building both soft and practical skills, aiming to improve employment prospects and foster positive personal development among participants.

The current evidence base for the effectiveness of employment programmes in reducing youth crime is not very strong. The available evidence suggests that the impact of employment programmes on youth offending is quite modest. According to recent reviews, such schemes show a small positive effect on reducing violence-related offences and the likelihood of offending, but they do not make a significant difference across all outcomes related to offending. 

The trial will examine whether a 6‑month paid employment placement with specialist supervision, followed by 3 months of post‑employment support from a pathway advisor, reduces reoffending among 16–18‑year‑olds who have already offended. In addition to this primary outcome, the study will explore whether the programme also improves a range of secondary outcomes, including reductions in behavioural and overall difficulties, increases in self‑efficacy and positive work aspirations, improvements in employment status, and reductions in reoffending between 7 and 12 months after randomisation.

Who can participate?
Healthy volunteers aged 16-18 years referred via YOS. 

What does the study involve? 
The evaluation will collect baseline and 6-month, 9 month and 12-month follow-up data relating to YP in both intervention and control groups via a combination of an online questionnaire and administrative datasets. The primary outcome measured will be re-offending within 12-months. Data on re-offending will be obtained from the Police National Computer (PNC). The secondary outcomes relating to offending and NEET status will also be captured through administrative data sets. Secondary outcomes speaking to behavioural difficulties will be measured through the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire via an online survey. A self-reported self-efficacy scale will also be used as will questions relating to career/employment aspirations. Online surveys will be completed by participants with the process supported by Supervisors employed by TSM based within YOS. 
All participants will be offered a £20 voucher as an incentive for completing the baseline survey. Participants in the control group will be offered an £80 voucher as an incentive for completing the follow-up survey. 

The study includes an implementation and process evaluation (IPE) and a cost-consequence analysis as well as the study. The IPE will involve collecting both quantitative and qualitative data from YP in both intervention and control groups and from partners involved in the administration and implementation of the intervention. All YP will be invited to take part in a short survey at the end of the intervention period. The survey themes will include experiences and views of the Skill Mill programme (among the intervention group only); other services received (including business as usual services); and YPs goals and employment aspirations and their attitudes to violence and offending. YP will also be invited to take part in a qualitative interview at the end of their six-month employment placement. These interviews will explore their experiences of the programme, life experiences that have potentially impacted on their offending behaviour, and factors that have contributed to the achievement of outcomes. Interviewees will be given a £30 voucher for taking part in an interview. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Benefits and risks not provided at time of registration

Where is the study run from? 
The study is being run within YOS across 22 local authority areas across England and Wales, UK. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
The study will begin in March 2026 with four cohorts recruited across the following two years. Delivery of the intervention will be complete by May 2028. Data collection will be complete by September 2029. 

Who is funding the study? 
The Youth Endowment Fund, UK. 
 
Who is the main contact?
Dr Lucy Loveless (Principal Investigator), lucy.loveless@icf.com
Dr Aisha Ahmad (Project Manager), Aisha.Ahmad@icf.com

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 16-18 years old inclusive at the date of referral and date of engagement with the programme
2. Must have left school (completed year 11)
3. Offending history with one or multiple convictions for any type of offence
4. Will have received a youth justice board approved youth justice assessment such as asset plus or equivalent
5. Will be open, and active cases or and  recently closed cases
6. Must be willing and able to use public transport to get to the meeting point every day
7. Must be willing to work outdoors in all weathers as well as indoors
8. Must be willing to work towards gaining the cscs construction industry green card
Exclusion criteria:
1. Physical impairments that would prevent them from undertaking physical work of the kind that TSM is contracted to undertake
2. Substantial mental health issues that would prevent them from engaging in sustained employment or working within a team environment with other YP
3. Gang affiliations or personal history of violence such that YOS and TSM judge their inclusion to put at substantial risk the safety of other YP and/or supervisors and pathway advisors
4. Are not involved in any other trials of interventions running concurrently
